symbols.name: savings constant
symbols.meaning: The fixed positive constant $2^{-182}$ by which the logarithmic factor's exponent is reduced below 1.
symbols.quote: The power is $\kappa=2^{-182}$, a fixed positive number, so the time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

relations.quote: Integer multiplication below $n\lg n$ is the main theorem: a single deterministic Turing machine that runs in the [fixed-tape machine model](fixed-tape-model.md) multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly, with its logarithmic factor reduced by a fixed power.
It refutes the [n log n optimality conjecture](n-log-n-conjecture.md) in this model.
Multiplication is reduced to the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of the two integers' digit coefficients.
It relabels its axis positions by the [Chinese-remainder map](chinese-remainder-map.md).
Its movement is organized by [rank-saving recursion](rank-saving-recursion.md).
It computes its transforms on a [transform layout](transform-layout.md) that places the selected bits of each axis at a common offset.
The transform identity is based on the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), so permutations cancel instead of being sorted.
It chooses its source lengths as [prime source lengths](prime-source-lengths.md).

relations.predicate: converts the last cyclic coordinate by
relations.quote: It converts the last cyclic coordinate by a [phase twist](phase-twist.md).
It multiplies its records by [convolution over the polynomial ring](polynomial-ring-convolution.md).
It adds selected bits with [packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md).
It recovers its coefficients by [exact coefficient recovery](recovery-and-error.md), which rounds them to integers.
